title: ClayGraph G1d — Epochal Latent Field
core_findings: Historical Clay research restores the original requirement that memory can influence next cognition before explicit retrieval; this is compatible with G1c if implemented as cheap sparse latent activation rather than universal expensive traversal.
G1d separates authoritative truth, immutable resident semantic epochs, delta overlays, ephemeral latent activation and temporary epoch-pinned Assemblies.
Synthetic 30k-node delta tests show strong small-update savings but increasing query/memory tax; compaction should be workload-adaptive.
Synthetic 1,000-query epoch proxy had zero old/new snapshot mismatches.
Lazy local activation update measured 0.028 ms median vs 1.098 ms eager whole-field decay in the synthetic test, with about 5.2% final active nodes.
No current G1d promotion: actual corpus, target 4B, long-run field noise, concurrent crash/replay and live FRANK remain untested.
negative_results: global O(N) salience decay rejected as default
current spreading activation superiority remains unproven
highest_information_next_test: Matched no-field vs truthful-field vs shuffled-field experiment on events where explicit memory retrieval may not trigger; equalize final visible facts/order/token budget and test target 4B operation/answer effect.
frank_feedback: Add semantic epochs + sparse latent field + epoch-pinned Assembly experimentally inside M.MEMORY_FABRIC; keep exact/frame/workspace/effect authority boundaries unchanged.

summary: Historical Clay research revives the requirement that memory influences cognition before explicit retrieval, aligning with G1c via cheap sparse latent activation. G1d distinguishes authoritative truth, immutable semantic epochs, delta overlays, ephemeral activation, and temporary Assemblies, with synthetic 30k-node tests showing small-update savings but rising query/memory costs, while 1,000-query epoch proxies had zero snapshot mismatches. Lazy local activation updates measured 0.028 ms median (vs 1.098 ms eager decay), with ~5.2% active nodes, but G1d lacks promotion due to untested 4B corpus, long-run noise, and live FRANK. The highest-priority test compares no-field, truthful-field, and shuffled-field effects on implicit memory events at 4B scale.
